sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A small carnivorous rosette plant of wet sandy soils and acidic bogs, from the southeastern United States to tropical America. The rosette may reach about 12 cm across.

sections.title: Leaves and prey capture
sections.text: The leaves bear glandular tentacles tipped with sticky droplets. Small animals caught on them are digested by the leaf, supplementing nutrients absorbed from poor soil.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: This is not eaten as a food plant; the botanical sources consulted do not document safe food use.
